fp_criteria: Behavioral advertising SDK is present but explicitly disabled for users under 13 or identified minors; ads served are non-personalized only
Code includes explicit opt-out mechanisms or defaults to non-behavioral ad serving for under-18 users in compliance with PIPEDA guidelines
Code is example or documentation code showing deprecated practices; actual production code uses non-behavioral advertising only
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS age-gating that disables behavioral targeting for minors (non-personalized ads only), it's FP.
If ads are served without behavioral profiling or interest-based targeting, it's FP.
If behavioral advertising is active or configurable for users of any age in minor-facing code, flag as TP.

rules.name: Consent Flow Without Simplified Explanation for Teens
rules.description: PIPEDA meaningful consent guidelines require that teens (13-17) can understand the consequences of consent. Complex multi-step consent flows with dense legal text may fail the meaningful consent test.
rules.fix_suggestion: Ensure consent flows for teen users include simplified, age-appropriate explanations. The OPC requires that the individual can understand what they are consenting to — complex legal language fails this test for teens.
rules.penalty: OPC compliance orders; Federal Court orders up to $100K CAD per violation

knowledge.plain_description: PIPEDA requires 'meaningful consent' for data processing, which for teens (13-17) means they must reasonably understand the consequences of their consent. Complex, multi-step consent flows or dense legal language may fail this test and undermine the validity of consent.
tp_criteria: Consent flow for teens presents dense legal language, multi-layered terms, or complex privacy policies without plain-language summaries or visual aids to aid understanding
Consent requests are bundled together without allowing granular consent choices; teens must accept all data uses or none
Consent process includes confirmation steps, timeout delays, or UI friction that obscures the actual data practices being consented to
fp_criteria: Consent flow uses plain language appropriate for ages 13-17, with visual explanations of what data is collected and how it's used
Teens are presented with granular consent choices (e.g., separate toggles for analytics, ads, location) allowing them to understand and control each processing purpose
Consent explanation is concise, with links to more detail but not requiring reading dense terms to proceed
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS plain-language, age-appropriate consent with granular choices for teens, it's FP.
If consent flow uses visual aids, summaries, and clear language understandable to 13-17 year olds, it's FP.
If consent requires accepting dense legal text or doesn't explain data practices in plain language, consider TP but note Compliance Determining: False (guidance-level rule).

rules.name: Missing Parental Consent for Under-13 Data Collection
rules.description: OPC position: children under 13 cannot provide meaningful consent. Parental consent is required for all personal data collection from users under 13.
rules.fix_suggestion: Implement verifiable parental consent before collecting any personal data from users under 13 in Canada.
rules.penalty: OPC compliance orders; Federal Court orders up to $100K CAD per violation

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects when an application collects personal data from users under 13 without obtaining explicit parental consent first. Under PIPEDA and OPC guidance, children under 13 cannot legally provide their own consent for data collection, making parental authorization a mandatory legal requirement.
tp_criteria: Code actively collects personal data (name, email, location, device ID, behavioral data) from users identified or reasonably inferred to be under 13
Collection mechanism exists but contains no parental consent flow, verification, or gate before data is stored or transmitted
Application processes or stores collected data from under-13 users without documented evidence of prior parental authorization
fp_criteria: Code implements a parental consent verification flow (email confirmation, ID verification, or account gate) that blocks under-13 data collection until consent is obtained
Data collection is limited to anonymized telemetry or aggregate analytics that cannot identify individual children
Code exists in test/mock mode, vendor libraries, or admin-only sections not exposed to end users
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS parental consent gating before any personal data is collected or stored, it's FP.
If data collection is intentionally restricted to users 13+ (via age gate or verification), it's FP.
If the codebase contains only import statements, type declarations, or non-functional consent UI components without backend enforcement, it's FP.

rules.name: Data Collection Beyond Reasonable Purpose for Minors
rules.description: PIPEDA Section 5(3) requires that data collection serve purposes a 'reasonable person' would consider appropriate. For minors, the OPC applies a higher standard — marketing, profiling, and engagement optimization may fail this test.
rules.fix_suggestion: Review all data collection purposes for minors against the 'reasonable person' test. Marketing, profiling, and engagement optimization for children may be deemed inappropriate under PIPEDA.
rules.penalty: OPC compliance orders; Federal Court orders up to $100K CAD per violation

knowledge.plain_description: This rule identifies data collection practices that exceed what a reasonable person would consider appropriate for minors, particularly marketing, behavioral profiling, and engagement optimization tactics. PIPEDA applies a stricter 'reasonable person' standard for children than for adults.
tp_criteria: Code implements behavioral profiling, micro-targeting, or personalized advertising specifically to minors based on their usage patterns or inferred preferences
Collected data is used for engagement optimization (nudges, notifications timed to re-engage) or persuasive design tactics targeting minors
Collection includes sensitive data (location, browsing history, app usage, device identifiers) that serves marketing or profiling purposes rather than core service functionality
fp_criteria: Data collection directly enables core service functionality (e.g., username for account recovery, location for navigation in a maps app)
Profiling or analytics are used only to improve product stability, security, or accessibility features—not engagement or revenue optimization
Code is documentation, design specification, or disabled/stub implementation not actively used by the product
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code collects data ONLY to provide the primary service and NOT for marketing, profiling, or engagement optimization, it's FP.
If data usage is limited to A/B testing product stability or accessibility improvements (not user retention), it's FP.
If the collection scope would be considered reasonable for an adult (e.g., basic analytics), but the minor context makes it unreasonable due to higher susceptibility to persuasion, it's TP.

rules.name: Missing Parental Consent for Under-14 Data Collection
rules.description: South Korea PIPA Article 22-2 requires parental/guardian consent for processing personal data of children under 14. This extends COPPA's threshold by one year — children aged 13 need parental consent in South Korea.
rules.fix_suggestion: For South Korean users, parental consent is required for children under 14 (not under 13 as in COPPA). Update age thresholds to 14 for Korean deployments.
rules.penalty: Up to 3% of global revenue

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects missing parental consent for children under 14 in applications subject to South Korea's PIPA. Unlike COPPA (which sets the threshold at 13), PIPA extends the requirement to age 14, meaning children aged 13 require parental consent in South Korea.
tp_criteria: Code processes personal data from users identified or reasonably inferred to be under 14 without a parental consent mechanism
Data collection path exists with no age verification gate or parental authorization before personal data is collected, stored, or transmitted
Application persists collected data from under-14 users without documented parental consent token, verification record, or authorization timestamp
fp_criteria: Code implements age verification and parental consent flow (email verification, guardian account linkage, ID verification) that gates all personal data collection for users under 14
Application is restricted to 14+ users via account creation rules and age gate enforcement
Code is vendor-provided SDK, test fixture, or admin-only backend not exposed to user-facing data collection
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS parental consent verification and blocks under-14 data collection until consent is confirmed, it's FP.
If the application enforces an age gate at registration that limits access to 14+, and data collection only occurs post-gate, it's FP.
If data processing is limited to metadata or session state that doesn't constitute 'personal data' under PIPA (e.g., stateless request IDs), it's FP.

rules.name: Privacy Notice Without Child-Appropriate Language (Under 14)
rules.description: South Korea PIPA Article 39-3 §5 requires privacy information to be presented in clear, understandable language for children under 14. Generic adult privacy policies fail this requirement.
rules.fix_suggestion: Provide a separate, simplified privacy notice written in clear language understandable by children under 14. Do not present adult legal text as the sole privacy information.
rules.penalty: Up to 3% of global revenue

knowledge.plain_description: This rule flags privacy notices that use adult-level language, legal jargon, or complexity inappropriate for children under 14 in South Korea. PIPA Article 39-3 §5 mandates that privacy information be presented in clear, child-friendly language that minors can actually understand.
tp_criteria: Privacy notice or policy is displayed to users under 14 but uses complex legal terminology, dense paragraphs, or passive constructions typical of adult privacy policies
Notice lacks child-specific explanations of what data is collected, why, how it's used, or how long it's kept—using language above an age-appropriate reading level
Application shows the same privacy notice to both children and adults without adaptation, simplification, or child-friendly version for users under 14
fp_criteria: Code implements a separate, simplified privacy notice specifically for users under 14 using short sentences, concrete examples, and age-appropriate vocabulary
Privacy information is presented via interactive onboarding (visual diagrams, animations, question-and-answer format) designed for children's comprehension
Notice is internal documentation, developer comments, or legal team draft not shown to end users in the product interface
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code displays a child-specific privacy notice with simplified language and concrete examples for users under 14, it's FP.
If the same complex legal notice is shown to all ages without a child variant, it's TP regardless of how clear it might be for adults.
If privacy information is presented only in text form to adults but includes visual, interactive, or simplified formats for children, it's FP.

rules.name: Data Retained Beyond Service Period for Minors
rules.description: South Korea PIPA requires that personal information of children be deleted without delay when the purpose of collection has been achieved. Extended retention of children's data requires justification.
rules.fix_suggestion: Delete children's personal data promptly when the purpose of collection is achieved. Do not retain children's data indefinitely. Implement automatic retention limits.
rules.penalty: Up to 3% of global revenue

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects extended retention of children's personal data beyond the service period without documented justification. South Korea's PIPA requires that children's data be deleted promptly when the original collection purpose is fulfilled, unless there is a legal basis for retention.
tp_criteria: Code stores personal data from users under 14 and applies a retention policy longer than necessary to fulfill the primary service purpose (e.g., keeping contact info 2 years after account closure)
Retention logic contains no automatic deletion mechanism, expiration trigger, or user-initiated deletion option for children's data
Application lacks documented justification or legal basis (e.g., tax law, fraud investigation) for extended retention of minors' personal data
fp_criteria: Code implements automatic deletion of children's data when the service purpose ends (e.g., account closure triggers 30-day deletion or immediate anonymization)
Retention period is mandated by law (tax records, financial regulations) and retention logic includes child-specific handling aligned with PIPA minimization principles
Data retention code is administrative-only, test fixture, or applies only to anonymized or aggregate data that cannot identify individuals
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS automatic deletion or anonymization of children's data upon service conclusion, it's FP.
If retention periods for children match those for adults without child-specific minimization, it's TP.

If the codebase shows legal justification for extended retention (e.g., conditional holds for compliance) with specific documentation, evaluate whether the justification meets PIPA's strict child-data retention standard.

rules.name: Social Comparison Metrics Visible to Minors
rules.description: Displaying like counts, follower counts, or leaderboard rankings to children enables social comparison, which the AAP and WHO link to anxiety, depression, and self-esteem issues in minors.
rules.fix_suggestion: Hide or disable social comparison metrics (likes, followers, view counts, leaderboards) for users under 18. Consider removing public metrics entirely or showing them only to the content creator.
rules.penalty: Ethical design advisory — correlates with AADC Standard 5 (detrimental use), DSA Article 28, CAADCA dark pattern provisions

knowledge.plain_description: This rule identifies when applications display social comparison metrics (likes, follower counts, leaderboard rankings) to minors. Research from the AAP and WHO links social comparison metrics to increased anxiety, depression, and self-esteem damage in children, making this a behavioral health risk.
tp_criteria: Application displays like counts, comment counts, follower/subscriber numbers, or engagement metrics to child users in a way that enables social comparison
Leaderboards, rankings, or tier systems are visible to minors and explicitly show other users' scores, achievements, or performance metrics for comparison
Code renders social metrics prominently in feeds, profiles, or activity streams where children can see and compare their own metrics against peers
fp_criteria: Social metrics are visible only to the content creator/owner (e.g., creator analytics dashboard) and hidden from viewers, preventing social comparison
Metrics are disabled or hidden for users under a specified age (e.g., under 13 or under 16) via feature flag or role-based access control
Code implements metrics in documentation, design mockups, or admin-only analytics panels not exposed to child end-users
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code HIDES social metrics from minors while showing them to adults (via age-gated toggle or role restriction), it's FP.
If metrics are visible but anonymized or aggregated (no individual rankings or identifiable peer comparisons), it's FP.
If the application is explicitly restricted to adults 18+ and metrics are shown only within that age-gated context, it's FP.

rules.name: Missing Natural Stopping Cues in Content Feed
rules.description: Content feeds, playlists, or game sessions without natural stopping points (end screens, session limits, break prompts) encourage compulsive use. AAP guidelines recommend built-in stopping cues for children's products.
rules.fix_suggestion: Implement natural stopping cues: end-of-content screens, session time limits, break prompts ('You've been watching for 30 minutes'), or 'Good Night' modes. Do not allow infinite content consumption without intervention.
rules.penalty: Ethical design advisory — correlates with DSA Article 28 (addictive design), AADC Standard 5

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects content feeds, playlists, and game sessions that lack natural stopping points or session limits for minors. AAP guidelines recommend built-in stopping cues (end screens, episode limits, session timers) to reduce compulsive use and encourage healthy engagement patterns in children.
tp_criteria: Infinite scrolling feeds or auto-playing content streams are implemented for minors with no end screen, break prompt, or session limit
Game or play session continues indefinitely without natural conclusion, level caps, or prompts to take a break or stop
Playlist or video queue auto-advances through content without a stopping point where the child must consciously choose to continue
fp_criteria: Code implements session limits, break reminders, or end screens that prompt children to stop or take breaks after a set time or activity
Content feeds show a defined end (e.g., 'you've reached the end of today's stories') or daily reset mechanisms that create natural stopping points
Stopping cue features are configurable by parents/guardians and enabled by default for users under a specified age threshold
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS time-based session limits, break prompts, or end-of-content screens for minors, it's FP.
If auto-play or infinite scroll is enabled but only for users 18+, and disabled or limited for younger users, it's FP.
If stopping cues exist in design docs but are not enforced in the actual codebase, it's TP.

rules.name: Missing Parent Usage Dashboard
rules.description: Children's products should include a parent-facing dashboard showing usage statistics, time spent, and content accessed. This dashboard should be PIN-protected and not invasively profile the child.
rules.fix_suggestion: Implement a PIN-protected parent dashboard showing usage time, content accessed, and activity summaries. Ensure the dashboard provides oversight without invasive psychometric profiling of the child.
rules.penalty: Positive design advisory — correlates with AADC Standard 11 (parental controls), AADCA parental tools requirement

knowledge.plain_description: This rule flags children's applications lacking a parent-facing dashboard to monitor child usage, time spent, and content accessed. Best practice dashboards are PIN-protected, provide transparency without invasive micro-tracking, and empower parents to make informed decisions about their child's app engagement.
tp_criteria: Application is explicitly marketed as a children's product or service but lacks any parent dashboard, monitoring interface, or usage reporting feature
Parent dashboard exists but displays invasive real-time location tracking, keystroke logs, or message content monitoring rather than aggregate usage data
Dashboard is accessible without authentication (no PIN, password, or parent account linkage), allowing children to view or modify their own usage restrictions
fp_criteria: Application implements a PIN-protected or parent-account-authenticated dashboard showing usage time, content accessed, and feature usage without micro-tracking child behavior
Dashboard provides controls for screen time limits, bedtime modes, or content restrictions that parents can configure
Application is restricted to adult-only contexts (18+) or explicitly designed for non-parent-supervised use, making a dashboard unnecessary
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS a parent dashboard with usage statistics and parental controls, it's FP.
If a dashboard exists but is unprotected or easily bypassed by the child, it's TP despite the feature's existence.
If the application is not positioned as a children's product and has no age-targeting, lack of a parent dashboard is FP.

rules.name: Randomized Reward with Real-Money Purchase
rules.description: Loot boxes and gacha mechanics that combine randomized rewards with real-money purchases exploit variable-ratio reinforcement schedules. Multiple jurisdictions (Belgium, Netherlands, Australia) have classified these as gambling when targeting children.
rules.fix_suggestion: Do not combine randomized rewards with real-money purchases in children's products. Show exact contents before purchase, or use fixed reward systems. Multiple jurisdictions classify loot boxes as gambling when targeting children.
rules.penalty: Varies by jurisdiction — Belgium banned (criminal sanctions), Netherlands fined (up to €10M), Australia under review

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects loot boxes and gacha mechanics that combine randomized rewards with real-money purchases targeting minors. Belgium, Netherlands, Australia, and other jurisdictions classify these mechanics as gambling when targeting children due to their reliance on variable-ratio reinforcement and compulsive spending risk.
tp_criteria: Code implements randomized reward mechanics (loot boxes, gacha pulls, randomized item packs) where rewards are not guaranteed and rarity varies
Randomized rewards are purchasable with real money (in-app purchase, credit card, digital wallet) either directly or via premium currency
Application is marketed to or accessible to minors without age gates, and real-money purchase mechanics are not disabled or hidden from child users
fp_criteria: Randomized rewards are only purchasable with earned in-game currency that cannot be purchased with real money, removing the gambling element
Loot boxes or randomized mechanics are restricted to adults 18+ via age gate, and minors cannot access or purchase them
Application disables all randomized reward purchases for users under 16 or 18, replacing them with guaranteed-outcome alternatives
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code BLOCKS real-money spending on randomized rewards for users under 18, it's FP.
If randomized rewards exist but are only purchasable with earned currency (not real money), it's FP.
If the mechanics exist in game design documentation but are not implemented in purchasable code paths, it's FP.

rules.name: Social Media Account Allowing Under-16 Registration (Australia)
rules.description: Australia's Social Media Minimum Age Act 2024 prohibits users under 16 from holding social media accounts, effective December 10, 2025. Parental consent CANNOT override this ban. Platforms must take 'reasonable steps' to prevent under-16 registration.
rules.fix_suggestion: For Australian deployments, set minimum registration age to 16. Parental consent cannot override this requirement. Implement robust age verification — simple self-declaration is insufficient under the Act.
rules.penalty: Up to A$49.5 million (150,000 penalty units)

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects social media accounts that allow users under 16 to register or maintain active accounts in breach of Australia's Social Media Minimum Age Act 2024 (effective December 10, 2025). The law is absolute: parental consent cannot override the age restriction, and platforms must take reasonable steps to prevent underage registration.
tp_criteria: Application is a social media platform that accepts user registration without age verification and allows accounts for users under 16 to remain active
Age verification exists but is bypassable (e.g., self-reported age without proof, easy-to-fake ID upload, no backend validation) allowing under-16 users to create accounts
Platform does not implement reasonable age assurance measures and continues operating under-16 user accounts after December 10, 2025
fp_criteria: Code implements mandatory age verification (government ID verification, third-party age assurance service, or sufficiently robust identity checks) that blocks account creation for users under 16
Application is not a social media platform as defined by the Act (e.g., it's a messaging app, gaming platform, or educational tool without social media features)
Platform automatically deactivates or suspends accounts identified as belonging to under-16 users, with documented age-checking mechanisms in place
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS robust age verification that blocks under-16 registration, it's FP.
If age verification exists but is weak or easily circumvented (self-reported age only, no ID checks), it's TP.
If the application is not a social media platform per the Act's definition, lack of age restrictions is FP. The Act specifically targets social media platforms, not all online services.

rules.name: Missing Platform Age API Integration
rules.description: ASAA requires app stores and developers to integrate platform-native age APIs (Apple Declared Age Range API, Google Play Age Verification) during account creation and onboarding. Account creation flows that do not call these APIs leave teen users (13-17) unverified, violating TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Integrate Apple's Declared Age Range API (DeviceCheck framework) or Google Play Age Verification API into your account creation flow. Query the platform age signal before completing registration and branch logic for users identified as under 18.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects account creation or onboarding flows that fail to call platform-native age verification APIs (Apple Declared Age Range API or Google Play Age Verification). ASAA compliance requires these APIs to verify teen users (13-17) during signup, as required by multiple state laws.
tp_criteria: Account creation flow exists but contains no calls to Apple's Declared Age Range API or Google Play age verification endpoints
Onboarding process that collects user information for minors but bypasses or skips age API integration entirely
Code explicitly disables, comments out, or conditionally avoids platform-native age API calls during user registration
fp_criteria: Code imports or references age API libraries but implementation is in test/mock files or unit test suites
Age API call is present in the actual onboarding flow, even if wrapped in optional feature flags
App is admin-only or backend service that does not handle end-user signup or app installation
Documentation or comments describing age API integration without actual implementation is acceptable as design spec
rule_logic: If the onboarding code path IMPLEMENTS platform age API integration (Apple or Google), classify as FP

If age verification is deferred to a third-party service that itself calls platform APIs, check if the app directly orchestrates the platform API call; if not, verify third-party integration is mandatory fallback per asaa-av-003
If the app is adult-only or explicitly excludes minors from signup, platform age API integration is not required (FP)

rules.name: Raw DOB Storage Instead of Age Tokens
rules.description: ASAA and data minimization principles require apps to store age verification tokens or age bands rather than raw dates of birth. Storing date_of_birth or dob fields directly exposes sensitive PII and creates unnecessary liability under TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Replace raw DOB storage with an age verification token or age band (e.g., 'under-13', '13-17', '18+'). Compute the age category at verification time and discard the raw date. Store only the verification result and method.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects applications that store raw dates of birth (dob, date_of_birth fields) instead of age verification tokens or age bands. Storing unencrypted PII directly violates data minimization principles and increases liability under ASAA regulations.
tp_criteria: Database schema or code persists a date_of_birth, dob, or birth_date field in plaintext or simple encryption without tokenization
Age verification flow stores the user's raw birth year or full birth date instead of an age band (e.g., '13-17', 'adult') or opaque token
Code writes user age information to storage (database, SharedPreferences, UserDefaults, localStorage) without hashing or tokenizing via the platform's age API
fp_criteria: Raw DOB is stored only in test fixtures, mock data, or unit test setup code
Documentation or schema definition mentions DOB but no actual code persists it to production storage
App is admin-only backend that does not interact with end-user age data
Code stores DOB temporarily in memory for immediate age calculation and then discards it without persisting to disk
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS age tokenization or stores only age bands/tokens instead of raw DOB, classify as FP
If age verification is delegated to platform APIs that return opaque tokens and the app only stores those tokens, classify as FP
Temporary in-memory use of DOB for instant calculation followed by immediate discard is acceptable; only persistent storage of raw DOB is a violation

rules.name: Missing Fallback Age Verification
rules.description: ASAA requires robust age verification that does not rely solely on self-declaration. When platform-native age APIs are unavailable or inconclusive, apps must fall back to a third-party age verification provider (e.g., Ondato, Veriff, Yoti). Age check flows without a fallback path leave gaps in compliance.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add a fallback age verification path using a certified third-party provider (Ondato, Veriff, Yoti, or equivalent). When platform age APIs return inconclusive results, redirect to the fallback provider before granting access.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects age verification flows that rely entirely on platform-native APIs without a fallback provider. ASAA requires a secondary, third-party age verification service (e.g., Ondato, Veriff, Yoti) for when platform APIs are unavailable, inconclusive, or the user declines platform verification.
tp_criteria: Age verification code path checks only platform API availability and returns a hard error or allows unverified access if the platform API is unavailable
No integration with third-party age verification provider exists in the codebase for cases where platform API fails or is inconclusive
Code that handles platform API failure (null response, timeout, user decline) does not redirect to or invoke a fallback age verification service
fp_criteria: Third-party age verification provider integration exists in code, even if not currently enabled or if behind a feature flag
Code contains configuration, imports, or API endpoint references to a third-party age verification service (Ondato, Veriff, Yoti, or similar)
Fallback logic is documented or stubbed out in comments indicating future implementation
App is for adult-only use and does not serve minors, making fallback verification unnecessary
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS a third-party age verification fallback handler, classify as FP, even if the fallback is conditionally enabled
If platform API failure is handled by gracefully degrading to explicit parental consent flow (asaa-vpc-004), that counts as an acceptable fallback
Fallback must be in the primary code path, not just in error logging or analytics handlers

rules.name: Inadequate Age Category Assignment
rules.description: COPPA only requires checks for users under 13, but ASAA extends protections to teens aged 13-17. Code that checks only for <13 (COPPA threshold) without a separate 13-17 category fails to apply ASAA teen protections required by TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add a teen age category (13-17) alongside the existing COPPA child category (<13). Implement separate permission levels: children (<13) require full COPPA compliance, teens (13-17) require ASAA parental consent and device linking, adults (18+) have standard access.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects age verification logic that only checks for users under 13 (COPPA threshold) without implementing a separate age category for teens aged 13-17. ASAA extends protections to teens, requiring apps to treat the 13-17 age band differently from adults.
tp_criteria: Age verification code contains only an if (age < 13) check without a distinct 13-17 age category or teen-specific treatment path
Code applies protections (parental consent, data restrictions) only to users under 13 and treats users 13-17 identically to adults
User age categorization uses only two buckets (child vs. adult/everyone else) without a middle teen tier for 13-17
fp_criteria: Code implements three or more age categories including an explicit 13-17 teen bucket, even if not all teen protections are applied uniformly
Age verification returns an age band (e.g., 'TEEN_13_17', '13-17') rather than a single boolean, indicating category awareness
Parental consent or teen-specific restrictions are applied to users 13-17 even if the logic doesn't explicitly name the 13-17 category
App explicitly targets only adults (18+) and excludes minors entirely, making multi-tier categorization unnecessary
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS separate handling for the 13-17 age band (via conditional logic, enum, or function parameters), classify as FP
COPPA-only compliance (age < 13) without teen category is insufficient; ASAA requires awareness of 13-17 as a distinct category
Simply storing an age_category field that includes '13-17' is FP; the category must be used to gate different protections

rules.name: Missing Retroactive Account Verification (Alabama)
rules.description: Alabama HB 161 uniquely requires retroactive age verification for existing user accounts by Oct 1, 2027. Apps must implement a re-verification flow for their existing user base, not just new signups. Lack of a retroactive verification migration or batch process violates this requirement.
rules.fix_suggestion: Implement a retroactive age verification flow for existing accounts. Create a migration that flags unverified accounts and prompts users to complete age verification on next login. Set a compliance deadline (Oct 1, 2027 for Alabama HB 161) and restrict unverified accounts after that date.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects Alabama HB 161-specific non-compliance: apps must implement retroactive age verification for existing user accounts by October 1, 2027, not just verify new signups. The absence of a batch re-verification process or migration flow for legacy accounts violates Alabama's requirement.
tp_criteria: App serves Alabama users but contains no batch process, scheduled job, or migration logic to re-verify existing accounts after a certain date
Age verification is implemented only for new account creation without any mechanism to prompt or re-verify users who signed up before age verification was mandatory
Code has no reference to the Alabama HB 161 deadline (Oct 1, 2027) or any retroactive verification trigger for legacy accounts
fp_criteria: Codebase contains a batch verification job, scheduled task, or retroactive verification flow for existing users
App includes a 'reverify_age' or 'retroactive_verification' endpoint or function that can be invoked on existing accounts
Documentation or code comments reference Alabama HB 161 retroactive requirements and describe a planned or in-progress migration
App is not in Alabama's jurisdiction or explicitly does not serve Alabama users
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS or schedules a retroactive re-verification process for existing users, classify as FP
Retroactive verification must be active or scheduled before the October 1, 2027 deadline; simply having the infrastructure is insufficient if not triggered
Alabama-specific rules apply only to apps that target Alabama users; geofencing or explicit state targeting must be verified

rules.name: Free App Without Consent Flow
rules.description: ASAA requires verifiable parental consent before a minor (under 18) can download or install a free app. Download and install handlers that do not gate on parental consent violate TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add a parental consent gate before allowing free app downloads for users identified as minors. The consent mechanism must be verifiable (not just a checkbox). Consider using platform-native parental consent flows (Ask to Buy on iOS, Family Link on Android).
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects free apps that allow minors to download or install without verifiable parental consent. ASAA requires apps to gate download/installation on confirmed parental approval for users under 18, not just age verification alone.
tp_criteria: Download or installation handler does not check parental consent status before completing the download for a user identified as under 18
Code allows app installation to proceed immediately after age verification returns 'minor' status without requiring additional parental consent flow
Installation completion logic bypasses or skips parental consent gates when the user is under 18
fp_criteria: Download/install flow contains a parental consent check or requires guardian approval before installation completes
App routes minors to a parental consent flow (asaa-vpc-004, asaa-vpc-005) before allowing download to finalize
App is paid-only or requires account creation before download, which inherently gates access
App explicitly targets adults only and blocks users under 18 at the app store level or during onboarding
Code is in test suite, mock app store handler, or documentation of the intended flow
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS parental consent verification before completing app download/installation for minors, classify as FP
Download permission and parental consent are separate gates; passing age verification is not sufficient without consent verification
For free apps, the download action itself must be gated; consent can be deferred to first launch only if the download itself is blocked

rules.name: Missing In-App Consent Triggers
rules.description: ASAA extends parental consent requirements to in-app purchases made by minors. Purchase flows that do not check for parental consent when the user is under 18 violate TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add a parental consent verification step to in-app purchase flows when the buyer is identified as a minor (under 18). Use platform-native purchase approval (Ask to Buy, Family Link) or implement a custom consent flow with verifiable parental identity.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects in-app purchase flows that do not verify parental consent when the buyer is under 18. ASAA requires apps to check that a minor's parent has approved the purchase before charging for digital goods or services.
tp_criteria: In-app purchase handler does not check parental consent status or parent approval before processing a payment from a user under 18
Purchase flow applies age-based pricing or restrictions but does not gate the actual transaction on parental consent
Code completes a purchase transaction for a minor without a recorded parental approval record (see asaa-vpc-005)
fp_criteria: Purchase handler contains a parental consent verification step before finalizing any transaction for minors
Code routes minors to a parental consent flow before charging, even if consent is obtained via email or device family settings
App integrates with platform payment systems (Google Play, App Store) that natively enforce parental controls and the app trusts the platform result
App is free-to-play and does not process payments for minors
Purchase code is in test fixtures or mock payment handlers
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS parental consent verification for minor purchases, classify as FP
Platform-native parental controls (Google Family Link, Apple Screen Time) can count as acceptable consent if the app trusts and respects the platform's decision
Free in-app items or cosmetics that do not charge do not require parental consent

rules.name: Data Sharing Without Parental Approval
rules.description: ASAA requires parental consent before sharing a minor's data with third parties. Features that enable data sharing, analytics opt-in, or social sharing without checking parental consent status violate TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Gate all data sharing features behind a parental consent check for minor accounts. Require verifiable parental approval before enabling analytics opt-in, social sharing, or third-party data transfers. Log the consent decision with timestamp and method.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects data sharing, analytics, or social features that allow sharing a minor's data with third parties without verifiable parental consent. ASAA requires explicit parental approval before any minor data is shared beyond the app operator.
tp_criteria: Data sharing handler (to advertisers, analytics providers, social networks) does not check parental consent status before sending minor user data
Analytics opt-in or social sharing feature is enabled by default for minors without requiring parental approval
Code sends user data to a third-party service (Firebase, Mixpanel, Facebook SDK, etc.) without first verifying parental consent for minors
fp_criteria: Data sharing code checks parental consent status and blocks sharing if consent is not present
Analytics or third-party data sharing is disabled by default for minors unless parental consent is explicitly obtained
App disables all third-party data sharing for users under 18, with no option to share even with parental consent
Data sharing only occurs with first-party services owned by the app operator that are not third-party integrations
Code is in test files or mock analytics handlers
Documentation describes intended parental consent flow without implementation
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS parental consent checks before third-party data sharing for minors, classify as FP
First-party data retention (app operator's own servers) may not require parental consent; only third-party sharing does
Anonymized or aggregated data that cannot identify an individual user may not require parental consent, but ASAA is conservative—verify context

rules.name: Inadequate Consent Verification Method
rules.description: ASAA requires verifiable parental consent, meaning a simple checkbox or click-through is insufficient. Consent flows that rely solely on a checkbox, toggle, or single-click confirmation do not meet the verifiable consent standard required by TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Replace checkbox-based consent with a verifiable method: credit card transaction, government ID verification, video call verification, or signed consent form. The FTC's COPPA verifiable consent methods are the minimum standard. Store the verification method used alongside the consent record.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects parental consent flows that use insufficient verification methods, such as a simple checkbox or single-click confirmation. ASAA requires verifiable parental consent, meaning the parent must authenticate or prove identity, not just click a box.
tp_criteria: Parental consent flow consists of a single checkbox, toggle, or click-through confirmation without any parent authentication or identity verification
Consent is obtained by asking the user 'Is your parent okay?' or similar self-declaration without contacting the parent directly
Code obtains 'consent' without any method to verify that the person giving consent is actually the parent (e.g., no email confirmation, no identity check)
fp_criteria: Consent flow requires parent email confirmation, SMS verification, or other out-of-band authentication before consent is recorded
Code implements parental ID verification, government ID check, or credit card verification as part of the consent flow
Parental consent is obtained via device-level parental controls (Google Family Link, Apple Screen Time) where the OS verifies the parent's identity
Consent flow sends a verification link or code to a parent email address and requires parent to click/enter it
App uses a third-party parental consent provider (e.g., Veriff for parental ID verification)
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS any authentication or identity verification for the consenting parent, classify as FP
Simple acknowledgment without parent identity verification is insufficient; 'verifiable' means the app can demonstrate the parent actually approved
Out-of-band verification (email, SMS, device unlock) is more verifiable than in-app clicks; prefer these methods

rules.name: Missing Consent Record Persistence
rules.description: ASAA requires apps to maintain proof of verifiable parental consent. Consent flows that do not persist the consent record (timestamp, method, parent identity) to durable storage fail audit requirements under TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Persist all consent records to durable storage with: timestamp, consent method (e.g., credit card, ID verification), parent/guardian identifier, minor account identifier, and consent scope. Records must be retained for the lifetime of the account plus 3 years.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: This rule detects parental consent flows that do not persist consent records to durable storage. ASAA requires apps to maintain audit-able proof of parental consent, including timestamp, method, and parent identity, for compliance verification.
tp_criteria: Parental consent is obtained but not persisted to any durable storage (database, file system, secure enclave)
Consent record exists in memory or session but is not saved to disk or a backend database after consent is given
Code approves a minor action based on parental consent without recording when, how, or from whom the consent was obtained
fp_criteria: Consent record is persisted to a database or file system with at minimum: timestamp, consent method, and parent identity/contact
Consent is stored locally (SharedPreferences, UserDefaults, localStorage) with sufficient detail to reconstruct the consent event
Backend service persists consent records in a durable database with audit trail and encryption
App implements consent revocation records, showing when consent was withdrawn and by whom
Consent records are included in user data export (CCPA/GDPR) demonstrating persistent storage
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS persistent storage of consent records with timestamp and method, classify as FP
Consent persistence must outlive app session; memory-only storage does not satisfy durability requirement
Parent identity must be recorded (email, phone, device ID, or account ID); timestamp and method are also mandatory

rules.name: Missing Parent Account Linking
rules.description: ASAA requires minor accounts to be linked to a verified parent or guardian account. Account creation flows for minors that do not bind to a parent/guardian account violate the device-to-parent linking requirements of TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Require a parent/guardian account link during minor account creation. Store parentId or guardianId as a required foreign key on minor accounts. Use platform family APIs (Apple Family Sharing, Google Family Link) where available.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA requires minor accounts to be linked to a verified parent or guardian account during account creation. Apps that allow minors to create accounts without establishing this parent-child relationship violate device-to-parent linking requirements in TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
tp_criteria: Code path allows minor account creation to complete without requiring parent account linkage
Account creation flow for users under age threshold has no conditional logic checking for parent account binding
Database schema for minor accounts contains no foreign key or reference field to parent account
fp_criteria: Code implements parent account linking logic (even if optional, in-progress, or in test environment)
Function is part of test suite, mock implementation, or documentation example
Code is in admin-only or backend service that bypasses minor user flows (e.g., bulk account provisioning for schools)
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS mandatory parent account linkage in the minor account creation path, it's FP
If code only shows data structures for parent linking without enforcement in the creation flow, treat as TP

rules.name: No Cross-Platform Family Linking
rules.description: ASAA device-to-parent linking must work across platforms. Family linking implementations that are hardcoded to a single platform (iOS-only or Android-only) leave users on other platforms without required parental oversight, violating the multi-platform intent of TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Implement cross-platform family linking that works on both iOS (Family Sharing) and Android (Family Link). Provide a platform-agnostic fallback (email/SMS verification) for web and other platforms. Store family relationships in your backend, not just platform-native APIs.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA family linking must function across iOS, Android, and web platforms. Implementations that only support parental linking on one platform (e.g., iOS-only) leave users on other platforms without required parental oversight.
tp_criteria: Parental linking API is gated by platform check that explicitly allows only iOS OR only Android
Family linking feature is implemented in platform-specific code with no cross-platform shared service or API
Configuration or feature flag explicitly disables family linking on specific platforms
fp_criteria: Code implements cross-platform family linking through shared backend API or cloud service
Platform-specific code is only for UI rendering; the linking logic is platform-agnostic
Code is in test utilities or documentation explaining multi-platform support
rule_logic: If family linking is implemented via a single platform-specific service with no Android/iOS/web equivalents, it's TP
If platform-specific code calls a shared backend API for linking, it's FP

rules.name: Missing Parental Dashboard API
rules.description: ASAA requires that parents have oversight of their minor's account activity. Apps managing minor accounts without API endpoints for parental monitoring (activity feed, usage stats, content review) fail the supervisory tool requirements of TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Create parental dashboard API endpoints that expose: minor's activity summary, usage statistics, content interaction history, and account settings. Authenticate parent access via the established parent-child account link. Include real-time and historical views.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA requires parents to have oversight tools for their minor's account activity. Apps that manage minor accounts without providing API endpoints or interfaces for parental monitoring (activity logs, usage statistics, content review) fail supervisory requirements.
tp_criteria: Minor account management exists with no API endpoints for retrieving activity feed, usage data, or content view logs
Parent dashboard or monitoring interface is absent from codebase entirely
Account activity is logged internally but no mechanism exists to expose this data to parent-linked accounts
fp_criteria: Code implements parental dashboard API endpoints that return activity feed, usage stats, or content logs
Parent account has methods to query child account activity (even if incomplete or in development)
Code is in documentation, API spec, or test mock showing intended parental monitoring structure
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS parental dashboard API endpoints, it's FP
If code logs minor activity but has no parent-accessible query interface, it's TP

rules.name: No Remote Pause/Audit Capability
rules.description: ASAA requires parents to have remote pause and review capabilities for their minor's accounts. Minor account management without parental pause, lock, or activity review functionality violates the supervisory requirements of TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Implement remote parental controls: account pause/unpause, session termination, activity log review, and content audit. These controls must be accessible from the parent's device without requiring access to the minor's device. Provide push notifications to parents for flagged activity.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA requires parents to remotely pause and audit their minor's account activity. Apps without parental pause, account lock, or activity review functionality violate supervisory requirements for minor account management.
tp_criteria: Parental account has no method to pause or suspend linked minor account activity
No remote lock or disable functionality exists for parent-controlled minor accounts
Parent interface lacks ability to review or audit recent activity logs of linked minor accounts
fp_criteria: Code implements parental pause, lock, or activity review endpoints for minor accounts
Parent account has methods to disable features or restrict access for linked children (even if partial)
Code is in admin panel or test environment demonstrating pause/audit capability
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS remote pause or review methods for parent accounts, it's FP
If parent account exists but has no pause/lock/audit methods, it's TP

rules.name: Missing Guardian Verification in Linking
rules.description: ASAA requires that parent-child account linking includes verification of the guardian's identity. Linking flows that connect accounts without verifying the parent's identity allow unauthorized adults to link to minor accounts, violating TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Verify guardian identity before completing parent-child account linking. Use multi-factor verification: email confirmation to a verified adult account, plus identity verification (government ID, credit card charge, or knowledge-based authentication). Log the verification method used.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA requires verification of guardian identity during parent-child account linking. Linking flows that connect accounts without identity verification allow unauthorized adults to link to minor accounts, violating device-to-parent requirements.
tp_criteria: Account linking function accepts parent-child connection without identity verification step
Linking flow has no call to identity verification service or age/ID confirmation method
Parent account can link to minor account based only on email match or password without additional identity proof
fp_criteria: Linking flow implements identity verification (ID check, third-party provider, platform API verification)
Code calls identity verification service or implements age/identity confirmation before accepting link
Code is in test suite mocking identity verification or documentation explaining verification process
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS guardian identity verification in the linking flow, it's FP
If linking simply matches credentials without identity verification, it's TP

rules.name: Missing Consent Timestamp Logging
rules.description: ASAA requires audit trails for all consent actions. Consent flows that do not log a timestamp and method of consent cannot demonstrate compliance during state attorney general inquiries. Required by TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Add timestamp and method logging to all consent recording flows. Each consent record must include: ISO 8601 timestamp, consent method (e.g., 'credit-card-verification', 'id-check'), parent identifier, minor identifier, and consent scope. Use server-side timestamps, not client-provided values.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA requires audit trails that log the timestamp and method of every consent action. Consent flows without this logging cannot demonstrate compliance to state attorneys general during regulatory inquiries.
tp_criteria: Consent action is recorded without capturing timestamp of when consent was given
Audit log for consent is created but does not include the method of consent (form submission, API call, voice, etc.)
Consent event handler has no logging or only logs boolean consent value without temporal data
fp_criteria: Code logs consent actions with both timestamp and method information
Audit trail function captures when and how consent was obtained (even if in test code)
Code is in documentation or test setup explaining timestamp and method logging structure
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS consent logging with timestamp AND method, it's FP
If consent is logged without timestamp or method, or not logged at all, it's TP

rules.name: Inadequate Retention Period
rules.description: ASAA audit trail requirements mandate that consent and verification records are retained for the lifetime of the account plus 3 years. Data retention policies with shorter periods (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) fail to meet the retention requirements of TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Set retention period for consent and age verification records to account lifetime + 3 years minimum. Do not apply automatic TTL or cleanup policies to compliance records. Implement a separate retention policy for ASAA audit data that overrides general data retention schedules.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA mandates retention of consent and verification records for the account lifetime plus 3 years. Data retention policies with shorter periods (90 days, 1 year) fail to meet regulatory requirements.
tp_criteria: Retention policy or code comment explicitly sets retention period less than account lifetime + 3 years
Data deletion function removes consent/verification records before account lifetime + 3 years threshold
Retention configuration in settings or database schema defines purge schedule shorter than required
fp_criteria: Retention policy specifies lifetime + 3 years or longer for consent/verification records
Code shows indefinite retention or policy that extends beyond required period
Code is in test/mock implementation or documentation; actual retention policy is elsewhere
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS or enforces retention policy of lifetime + 3 years or longer, it's FP
If retention period is explicitly shorter or no retention policy is defined, it's TP

rules.name: No Audit Trail Endpoint
rules.description: ASAA requires apps to provide compliance data to state attorneys general upon request. Apps storing consent and verification data without an API endpoint to export this data for regulatory inquiries cannot efficiently respond to AG requests, risking non-compliance with TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Create an authenticated API endpoint (e.g., /api/compliance/audit-trail) that exports consent records, age verification logs, and parental linking history in a structured format (JSON/CSV). Restrict access to authorized compliance officers. Include filtering by date range, user ID, and record type.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA requires apps to provide compliance data to state attorneys general upon request. Apps storing consent and verification data without an export API endpoint cannot efficiently respond to regulatory inquiries.
tp_criteria: Audit trail data is stored in database but no API endpoint exists to export or retrieve it
No export mechanism exists for compliance data in response to regulatory requests
Consent and verification records are accessible only through internal admin tools, not API
fp_criteria: Code implements API endpoint for exporting audit trail or compliance data
Export or data retrieval mechanism exists for regulatory authorities (even if in development)
Code is in test/mock or documentation describing intended export API structure
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS an audit trail export API endpoint, it's FP
If audit data exists but no export API is present, it's TP

rules.name: Missing Age Verification Method Logging
rules.description: ASAA audit requirements mandate recording which age verification method was used for each user. Age verification flows that do not log the specific method (platform API, ID verification, third-party provider) cannot demonstrate compliance methodology to state attorneys general.
rules.fix_suggestion: Log the age verification method alongside the verification result. Record: method type (platform-api, id-verification, third-party-provider), provider name (Apple, Google, Ondato, Veriff), confidence score, and timestamp. Store in the same audit trail as consent records.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA audit requirements mandate recording which age verification method was used for each user. Age verification flows that do not log the specific method (platform API, ID verification, third-party provider) cannot demonstrate compliance methodology.
tp_criteria: Age verification is performed but audit log does not capture which method was used
Age verification function has no logging call recording the verification method identifier
Audit trail records age as verified without storing the specific verification technique employed
fp_criteria: Code logs age verification events with the method identifier (e.g., 'platform_api', 'id_provider', 'third_party')
Audit function records which verification service or technique was used for age confirmation
Code is in test or documentation showing age verification method logging
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS logging of age verification method in audit trail, it's FP
If age verification occurs without method logging, it's TP

rules.name: Mutable Consent Records
rules.description: ASAA audit trail integrity requires consent records to be append-only and immutable. Consent logs that allow UPDATE or DELETE operations compromise the evidentiary value of the audit trail and violate the record integrity requirements implied by TX HB 18, AL HB 161, LA Act 440, and UT SB 142.
rules.fix_suggestion: Make consent and verification records append-only. Remove UPDATE and DELETE operations from consent log models. Use soft-delete with a revocation record instead of hard deletes. Consider an immutable ledger pattern (event sourcing) for maximum audit integrity. Add database-level constraints to prevent mutation.
rules.penalty: Up to $2,500 per violation per state; Alabama HB 161 includes retroactive compliance requirement by Oct 1, 2027

knowledge.plain_description: ASAA requires consent records to be append-only and immutable to maintain audit trail integrity. Consent logs that allow UPDATE or DELETE operations compromise evidentiary value and violate record integrity requirements.
tp_criteria: Consent audit table has UPDATE or DELETE triggers or methods that allow modification of existing records
Code contains conditional logic that modifies or deletes previously logged consent entries
Database schema for consent records lacks immutability constraints (e.g., no insertion-only table definition)
fp_criteria: Consent log table is configured as append-only with no UPDATE/DELETE permissions
Code uses immutable data structures or event sourcing pattern for consent records
Database schema explicitly prevents modification of historical consent entries
Code in test files, spec files, fixture files, or mock directories (__tests__/, test/, spec/, __mocks__/) — test code is never a real compliance violation.
rule_logic: If the code IMPLEMENTS append-only or immutable consent records (no UPDATE/DELETE), it's FP
If code allows UPDATE or DELETE on consent records, it's TP
